questions.prompt: Which of these questions is written so that it could be tested by a fair experiment?
options: Is a sunset more beautiful than a sunrise?
Does adding compost make bean plants grow taller?
Should farmers be paid more money?
What is the best song to play in a field?
questions.explanation: A testable question can be answered by changing one factor and measuring a result; beauty, fairness, and taste are opinions that cannot be measured.

questions.prompt: A student counts the number of beetles inside several quadrats placed in a meadow. The main reason for using many quadrats instead of just one is to:
options: Get a more representative estimate of beetle numbers
Change the number of beetles in the field
questions.explanation: Beetles are not spread evenly, so taking several samples and averaging them gives a more reliable, representative estimate of the whole area.

questions.prompt: A researcher claims that wearing a lucky bracelet makes crops grow better but says the effect cannot be detected by any measurement. Why would scientists reject this claim?
options: Because the claim cannot be tested or proven wrong
Because crops never grow in fields
Because only animals can be studied scientifically
questions.explanation: A scientific explanation must be falsifiable; if no observation could ever prove it wrong, it lies outside science.

questions.prompt: Which mineral ion is most needed to build strong bones and teeth?
questions.explanation: Calcium is an inorganic mineral ion used to make bones and teeth hard and strong; the other options are not minerals.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches an organic molecule group with its building block (monomer)?
questions.explanation: Nucleic acids such as DNA are polymers of nucleotides; proteins are made of amino acids and carbohydrates of sugars.

questions.prompt: A cell joins many glucose units into one long starch molecule. For every bond formed between two glucose units, the cell:
questions.explanation: Building a polymer is a condensation reaction: each new bond between monomers releases one water molecule.

questions.prompt: An enzyme that breaks down starch has no effect on protein. The lock-and-key model explains this because:
options: The active site only fits the shape of starch, not protein
Protein molecules are too small to be touched
The enzyme is used up before it reaches the protein
Enzymes can break down any molecule equally
questions.explanation: An enzyme is specific: its active site has a shape that fits only its own substrate, so a starch enzyme cannot act on protein.

questions.prompt: An enzyme works fastest at 37 degrees Celsius. At 10 degrees Celsius the reaction is much slower mainly because:
options: The enzyme has been denatured by the cold
Molecules move more slowly and collide less often
The active site has changed shape permanently
The substrate has turned into water
questions.explanation: Cold does not denature the enzyme; it simply slows molecular movement so enzyme and substrate meet less often, lowering the rate.

questions.prompt: Two enzymes from the human gut are tested across a range of pH. Enzyme X peaks at pH 2 and enzyme Y peaks at pH 8. The best conclusion is that:
options: Enzyme X works best in the acidic stomach and enzyme Y in the alkaline small intestine
Both enzymes work best in the stomach
pH has no effect on either enzyme
Enzyme Y is not really an enzyme
questions.explanation: Each enzyme has its own optimum pH matching where it works: pH 2 suits the acidic stomach, while pH 8 suits the more alkaline small intestine.

questions.prompt: Which structure controls what substances enter and leave every cell?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane surrounds every cell and controls the movement of substances in and out.

questions.prompt: A scientist finds a single-celled organism that has no true nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles. This organism is:
questions.explanation: Lacking a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles is the defining feature of prokaryotic cells such as bacteria.

questions.prompt: A cell is observed making large amounts of protein to export. Which two organelles would you expect to be especially numerous or active?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes build the proteins, and mitochondria supply the energy from respiration needed to make and export them.

questions.prompt: In which organelle does photosynthesis take place in a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, which contain the green pigment chlorophyll that traps light energy.

questions.prompt: Yeast used to ferment dough respires without oxygen. The products of this anaerobic respiration in yeast are:
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide; the carbon dioxide is what makes dough rise.

questions.prompt: On a bright sunny day, a leaf takes in carbon dioxide and gives out oxygen overall. At the same time the leaf is also respiring. The best explanation is that:
options: The leaf has stopped respiring during the day
Photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so there is a net release of oxygen
Oxygen and carbon dioxide are the same gas
questions.explanation: Plants respire all the time, but in bright light photosynthesis exceeds respiration, so the net gas exchange is oxygen out and carbon dioxide in.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the long molecule that carries the genetic instructions of an organism?
questions.explanation: DNA stores the genetic information that is passed from parents to offspring and directs how the cell works.

questions.prompt: In pea plants the allele for tall (T) is dominant over the allele for short (t). A plant with the genotype Tt will be:
options: Short, because it carries the t allele
Tall, because the dominant T allele is expressed
Medium height, a blend of both
questions.explanation: A dominant allele is expressed whenever it is present, so a heterozygous Tt plant shows the tall phenotype.

questions.prompt: Two pea plants that are both heterozygous tall (Tt) are crossed. Using a Punnett square, what fraction of the offspring are expected to be short (tt)?
questions.explanation: A Tt x Tt cross gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so one quarter of the offspring are short (tt).

questions.prompt: Which scientist is best known for the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed that species change over time through natural selection, often called survival of the fittest.

questions.prompt: A few beetles in a population are born with a colour that hides them from birds. Over many generations this colour becomes common. The best explanation is that:
options: The beetles chose to change their own colour
Birds taught the beetles to hide
Better-camouflaged beetles survived and passed on the helpful allele more often
All beetles changed colour at the same time
questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on existing variation: the camouflaged beetles survive and reproduce more, so the advantageous allele increases over generations.

questions.prompt: After an antibiotic is used widely, a population of bacteria becomes mostly resistant to it. Which statement best describes what happened?
options: The antibiotic caused each bacterium to become resistant on purpose
Resistant bacteria already existed and survived to reproduce, so resistance spread
All bacteria are always resistant to every antibiotic
questions.explanation: Random variation means some bacteria are already resistant; the antibiotic selects for them, and the survivors pass on resistance to their offspring.

questions.prompt: Which body system is mainly responsible for transporting oxygen and nutrients to all the cells of the body?
questions.explanation: The circulatory system uses the heart and blood vessels to carry oxygen, nutrients, and wastes around the body.

questions.prompt: After a meal of injera, which sequence correctly shows how energy from the starch reaches a muscle cell?
options: Starch is digested to glucose, glucose travels in the blood, the muscle cell respires it to release energy
Starch travels straight to the muscle and is breathed out
Glucose is made in the muscle by photosynthesis
Starch is turned into oxygen in the stomach
questions.explanation: Digestion breaks starch into glucose, the circulatory system carries the glucose to cells, and respiration in the muscle releases the stored energy.

questions.prompt: During hard exercise a person breathes faster and their heart beats faster. How do the respiratory and circulatory systems work together to support the muscles?
options: The lungs take in more oxygen and the blood delivers it to the muscles more quickly
The lungs make glucose and the heart digests it
The muscles stop needing oxygen during exercise
The heart removes oxygen from the blood
questions.explanation: Faster breathing brings in more oxygen, and a faster heartbeat speeds blood flow so oxygen and glucose reach the muscles for respiration.
